chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Hammad, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The menstruating woman recites the Quran and praises Allah.
ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman recite the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Kulayni in *Al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that menstruation does not prohibit Quranic recitation, resolving the juristic debate by distinguishing between ritual impurity (*hadath*) and ritual cleanliness (*taharah*). It underscores the Shia view that the restriction on recitation applies primarily to those in a state of major ritual impurity requiring full ablution or bathing, rather than excluding menstruating women entirely from engaging with the Divine Word.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Hammad, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The menstruating woman can recite the Quran and Praise Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Hammad from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Women while experiencing Hayd (menses) have permission to recite al-Quran and praise Allah.
